name: Mach nha
summary: Mạch nha is the malt from Mộ Đức. The Cẩm Thành ward article pairs it with Thi Phổ in the proverb and says it is eaten with rice paper. A second ward article prints the sprout-and-reduce method. No price was printed.
culture: The proverb on the Cẩm Thành ward article is kẹo gương Thu Xà, mạch nha Thi Phổ (Mộ Đức). The malt article on the same ward site says Địa chí Quảng Ngãi records a display at the Hue and Hanoi fairs around 1930–1935, and a rank of Cửu phẩm văn giai for a malt maker.
taste: The malt article calls traditional mạch nha lightly sweet and mild, not harsh if you eat a lot of it. A standard jar, it says, does not slump when tilted and does not stick to the hand.
howToEat: The ward article on sugar says mạch nha comes from fermenting starch in rice, cassava, or rice malt into maltose, and names bánh tráng spread with mạch nha.

The malt article quotes a three-stage process from Địa chí Quảng Ngãi: sprout the grain, cook and press and filter, then reduce. It says the reduction decides whether the malt is thick or thin. Eat it with rice paper. The same article also describes a separate cassava maltose.
Vietnam Airlines lists mạch nha among gifts and prints no method and no price.
No hour was printed. The hour is Check on arrival.
where: Mộ Đức and Thi Phổ, on the Cẩm Thành ward articles. Not the city center.
seoTitle: Mach nha — malt from Mo Duc
seoDescription: Mạch nha from Thi Phổ in Mộ Đức, eaten with rice paper. The ward article prints no price. Check on arrival.
